# ua-inspect

> Zero-dependency TypeScript User-Agent parser for Node.js, browsers, and edge runtimes. It reports browser, engine, operating system, device, CPU, non-browser client, and in-app context as stable lowercase ids, with `null` for unknown values.

Install with `npm install ua-inspect`.

## Imports

```ts
import { atLeast, describe, is, isBot, isIPad, isIPadOS, isInApp, isWebView, labels, parse } from 'ua-inspect';
import { parseRequest } from 'ua-inspect/server';
import { detect } from 'ua-inspect/browser';
```

`ua-inspect/check` exports the query helpers alone. `ua-inspect/labels` exports display names alone. Use the subpaths when you need the smallest bundle.

## Result contract

```ts
interface Version {
    full: string;
    major: number;
    minor: number | null;
    patch: number | null;
    toString(): string;
}

interface UAInfo {
    ua: string;
    browser: { name: string | null; version: Version | null; family: string | null; mode: string | null };
    engine: { name: string | null; version: Version | null };
    os: { name: string | null; version: Version | null };
    device: { type: string | null; vendor: string | null; model: string | null };
    cpu: { architecture: string | null; bitness: 32 | 64 | null };
    client: { type: string | null; name: string | null; token: string | null; version: Version | null };
    context: { type: string | null; name: string | null; app: string | null; version: Version | null };
}
```

- Every unknown value is `null`. There is no `"unknown"` sentinel.
- `Version` is `{ full, major, minor, patch, toString() }`. Use `atLeast(version, '130')` for a floor, or read `major`.
- `isIPad` covers the iPadOS id or the `iPad` model. `isIPadOS` narrows `os.name` to `'ipados'`.
- Ids are lowercase strings. `labels` maps an id to display text.
- `parse()` never throws. `detect()` throws outside a browser window or worker.
- `browser.name` and `browser.family` are independent. A Chromium fork with no catalog row is `{ name: null, family: 'chromium' }`.

## Recipes

```ts
// Block crawlers but keep a person's assistant.
const info = parseRequest(request);
if (is(info, { clientType: ['bot', 'crawler', 'ai-crawler'] })) {
    return new Response(null, { status: 403 });
}

// Phone or tablet.
if (is(info, { device: ['mobile', 'tablet'] })) { /* ... */ }

// Any Chromium brand: Chrome, Edge, Brave, Samsung Internet, forks.
if (is(info, { family: 'chromium' })) { /* ... */ }

// The iPad that the evidence actually names.
if (isIPad(info)) { /* ... */ }

// A null-safe version floor.
if (atLeast(info.browser.version, '130')) { /* ... */ }

// In-app context.
if (is(info, { context: 'line' })) { /* LINE in-app browser */ }
if (is(info, { app: 'line' })) { /* LINE in-app browser or LIFF */ }

// One-line summary for logs or UI.
describe(info); // 'Google Chrome 150.0.0.0 on Windows 10 (Desktop)'

// Host context.
if (isInApp(info)) { /* in-app browser or mini-app */ }
if (isWebView(info)) { /* browser.mode is webview */ }
```

## Pitfalls

1. `is(info, { browser: 'chrome' })` is false on a phone. Use `chrome-mobile` or `family: 'chromium'`.
2. `is(info, { os: 'ios' })` is false on an iPad. Use `['ios', 'ipados']` or `isIPad(info)`.
3. `info.browser.version > 120` is false. `Version` is an object. Use `atLeast()`.
4. `labels.browser[info.browser.name]` is `undefined` when no browser is known. Guard the id.
5. `parse(request)` returns all-null fields. Use `parseRequest(request)`.
6. `detect()` throws during SSR. Use `parse()` or `parseRequest()`.
7. `is(info, {})` is always true, and a misspelled key is ignored. Name real keys. Development builds warn.
